frontier.hypothesis: A second cross-jump merge point exists in the target - the /32 bgez join at code_label 99 or the loop exit - and it can carry a duplicated Judge-dependent statement byte-neutrally
frontier.mechanism: s4 proved four-arm duplication is re-merged at zero (indeed negative) byte cost by jump2; the kind-chain join failed only because none of its statements reads Judge. The /32 bgez join sits between the two Judge lookups, where a Judge-dependent statement IS in scope
frontier.next_probe: spell the /32 as an explicit if/else (both arms present, per s3's d32tern shape) and duplicate the obj+0x44 velocity store - or just its (&Judge)[...] subexpression via a named intermediate - into BOTH arms; measure vars= and bodydiff with INSTR=1 frame4.py. Also test the loop-exit join (a duplicated Judge-dependent statement in the break arm and after the loop).

frontier.hypothesis: The law is sites-1 rather than sites because exactly one folded address pseudo keeps a hard register; if that site can be made to orphan too, THREE lookup sites give vars=24
frontier.mechanism: lreg/greg assign a class to one of the folded address pseudos (its (use (reg N)) lands where a class can be inferred) while the others are left classless and go to reload1 alter_reg for a stack slot
frontier.next_probe: pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80030580 with tmp/grind/func_80030580/s3/var_j3read.c applied, then diff the .lreg/.greg entries for p110, p130 and the survivor to identify what class assignment distinguishes the one that keeps a register. A 3rd site costs +18 body vs the 4th's +25, so making the survivor orphan halves the remaining gap.

frontier.hypothesis: The target's vars=24 is not three 8-byte orphans but one orphan plus one untouched 16-byte slot (the phantom-frame-slots-gcc272 mechanism)
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 calls assign_stack_local for a computation it later register-allocates away; get_frame_size() counts it and no store is ever emitted. The three-orphan reading rests on an s2 corpus census of leaf functions, not on a direct measurement of this target
frontier.next_probe: sweep constructs that make cc1 assign a 16-byte stack object reload never touches - a DImode or larger-mode intermediate combine folds away, a struct-valued conditional, a chained struct assignment - accepting only variants with 0 ($sp) accesses and reading ctx= from the FRAMEDBG census (stack_temp / stack_local rather than spill_new would confirm the alternative decomposition).
